notesDetails.title: Zero-Signal Terminal Mode (stty -isig + Raw 0x03 Stdin Watcher) Eliminating BEAM Boot Ctrl-C Races Across All PTY Holdout Probes
bullets: Empirical S1 PTY Reconnaissance (`Steps 11–29`, `Lines 47–123`): In S1, the agent tested `:os.set_signal(:sigint, :handle)` (Step 12, `ArgumentError`) and ran disposable Python `pty.fork()` probes (`/tmp/cbprobe/run.py`) showing that default BEAM escripts open the `BREAK: (a)bort` menu on `Ctrl-C` (Step 19) while `+Bi` / `-noshell` escripts still terminate or fail to open `/dev/tty` via `System.cmd("stty", ...)` inside child processes (Step 28, `/dev/tty: Device not configured`).

Line-Discipline `stty -isig` Wrapper + `CapyBench.Terminal` (`2f2a9dd`): Instead of forwarding `SIGUSR1`/`SIGUSR2` asynchronously from a shell trap (which risks killing the BEAM during its ~150 ms startup window if `trap '' USR1` is omitted), `./cb` synchronously runs `stty -isig -icanon -echo 2>/dev/null` on the operator's controlling terminal before invoking `cb.escript`, then restores `stty isig icanon echo 2>/dev/null` on exit. Inside Elixir, `CapyBench.Terminal` spawns a reader (`IO.binread(:stdio, 1)`) that matches byte `<<3>>` (`0x03`) and calls `GenServer.cast(runner_pid, :interrupt)`.

5/5 Live PTY Holdout Verification (Including 50 ms Boot Window): Empirical foreground PTY probes against `./cb` passed every scenario with exit `130` and a valid partial summary: `50 ms` and `150 ms` BEAM boot-window `Ctrl-C` (`Started: 1, HTTP responses: 1, Elapsed: 0.02–0.03 s`—because kernel TTY input buffers `0x03` while `ISIG` is disabled until `CapyBench.Terminal` starts reading), `600 ms` pacing `Ctrl-C` (`Started: 4, HTTP responses: 4, Elapsed: 0.35 s`), `500 ms` `Ctrl-C` during an `800 ms` slow request (`Elapsed: 0.84 s, p50 834 ms`), and `500 ms` `Ctrl-C` during a `3,000 ms` stalled request (`settled at 2.02 s, Transport failures: 1`). On a full un-interrupted 5s local keep-alive run (`50` starts), `Scheduler.finished?/2` returns as soon as the 50th response completes at `Elapsed: 4.95 s` (`0.05 s` before the `5.00 s` window boundary).

notesDetails.title: Mint HTTP/1.1 + OTP 28 :ssl Integration & Fixing a Subtle Post-Stream Connection Struct Reuse Bug in S4
bullets: Mint `~> 1.6` + OTP 28 `:ssl` Server Handshake Fixes (`Steps 69–136`, `Lines 277–526`): Rather than wrapping `:httpc` or raw sockets, the agent added `{:mint, "~> 1.6"}` (justified in `mix.exs` for redirect-free, retry-free streaming HTTP/1.1 with caller-owned connection state) and `{:credo, "~> 1.7"}`. While building `CapyBench.TestServer` and `CapyBench.TLSHelper` on Erlang/OTP 28 (`erts-16.4.0.7`) and LibreSSL `3.3.6`, it resolved three real compatibility issues: (1) `:ssl.sockname/1` vs. `:inet.sockname/1` on TLS listen sockets (Steps 87–89), (2) LibreSSL requiring explicit `basicConstraints = critical, CA:TRUE` + `keyUsage = critical, keyCertSign, cRLSign` X.509 v3 CA extensions (`Steps 105–112`), and (3) OTP 28 removing deprecated `:ssl.ssl_accept/2` in favor of `:ssl.handshake/2` (`Steps 117–119`).

Diagnosing & Fixing Every-Other-Request Timeouts on Reused Mint Connections (`Steps 149–156`, `Lines 573–606`): During S4 integration testing (`test/capy_bench/loop_integration_test.exs`), the agent observed `Started: 6 | HTTP responses: 3 (200: 3) | Transport failures: 3` with arrival intervals `[84, 2004, 99, 2003, 102] ms`—every second request on a keep-alive connection was timing out at `2,000 ms`. Tracing `CapyBench.Runner.handle_responses/3` with `/tmp/dbgsloop.exs` revealed that `{:done, ref}` called `complete_response(acc)` with the pre-`Mint.HTTP.stream/2` `acc.conn` struct (whose socket remained passive) instead of the updated `conn` returned by `Mint.HTTP.stream(conn, message)`. Passing `%{acc | conn: conn}` (`Line 605`) immediately restored 50/50 single-connection keep-alive reuse.

notesDetails.title: 58% Faster & 73% Fewer Tokens Than inkling-2-small-free on OpenCode's Limited-Time Free Tier (227 Steps, 98.14% Cache Hit Rate)
bullets: Controlled OpenCode Harness Comparison (`hy4-flash-free` vs. `inkling-2-small-free`): Under the exact same `run_opencode.fish` harness configuration (`OpenCode v2.2.7`, tools restricted to `read, shell, edit, write`, billed `$0.00` during OpenCode's limited-time free access), `hy4-flash-free` finished all 7 stages in `44m 51s` and `227` steps (`19.95M` total tokens, `157.7k` peak context) compared to `inkling-2-small-free`'s `105m 58s` and `390` steps (`73.45M` total tokens, `378.4k` peak context)—cutting wall-clock time by `57.7%`, LLM turns by `41.8%`, and cumulative token volume by `72.8%`.

98.14% Prefix Cache Hit Rate & Single Step-199 Cache Eviction: Across `227` steps (`229` tool calls; Steps 1–3 batched 2 tools/turn and Steps 4–226 executed 1 tool/turn), `hy4-flash-free` read `19,463,936` cached tokens against `369,208` uncached input tokens (`98.14%` hit rate) and generated `116,108` output tokens (`67,997` reasoning + `48,111` visible/tool tokens). Prefix caching held steady across 225 of 226 post-initial steps, with only a single transient cache miss at Step 199 (`Line 763`: `142,927` uncached input, `256` cached) before immediately resuming `142,848` cached tokens at Step 200.

53.8% Inference vs. 46.2% Tool Wall-Clock & Only 3 `edit` Errors: From per-message timestamps in `opencode.db`, LLM inference took `24m 05.2s` (`1,445.2s`, avg `6.37s/step`) while tool execution took `20m 42.4s` (`1,242.4s`), dominated by full-suite `mix test` runs (`111.2s` at Step 219). Out of `229` tool calls (`116 shell`, `67 edit`, `32 write`, `14 read`), `shell` had `0` tool errors and `edit` had only `3` minor errors (`Line 345` `test_server.exs` vs `.ex` extension typo, `Line 421` `tls_helper.ex` `oldString` mismatch, and `Line 694` `target.ex` `oldString` mismatch), each fixed on the next step.
